payload.title: Resonance structures, bond order and bond length

stimulus.description: A student studies the species O₃, which has 18 valence electrons and is made of three O atoms. The central atom is bonded to every other atom.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Draw all of the Lewis structures of O₃ that obey the octet rule and show all valence electrons. Show that more than one acceptable structure exists.
parts.model_answer: Each of the 2 resonance forms has one O=O double bond and one O–O single bond, with the double bond in a different position in each of the two forms; all 18 valence electrons are shown with lone pairs on the outer atoms.

rubric_rows.criterion: Draws a correct Lewis structure that accounts for all 18 valence electrons with one O=O double bond and one O–O single bond
common_errors: omits lone pairs on the terminal atoms

rubric_rows.criterion: Shows the other resonance form(s), with the double bond in a different position (2 forms in total)

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Calculate the average bond order of the bonds from the central atom to the outer atoms.
parts.model_answer: Total bonds divided by the number of equivalent positions: (2 + 1)/2 = 1.50.

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates the average bond order of about 1.50
common_errors: gives the bond order as 2 or 1 for every bond

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Predict how the length of the bonds from the central atom to the outer atoms compares with the length of a typical single bond and a typical double bond between the same two elements. Justify your answer.
parts.model_answer: The bond lengths are all equal and between those of a single bond and a double bond, because the electrons are delocalized over all the equivalent positions and the average bond order is between 1 and 2.

rubric_rows.criterion: States that the bonds are equal in length and between the single-bond and double-bond lengths because the average bond order lies between 1 and 2
common_errors: says one bond is shorter than the others
